The '''HP Elite x2 1012 G2''' (Motherboard 82CA) is a 12.3" 2-in-1 detachable tablet PC powered by 7th generation Intel Core (Kaby Lake-Y / Kaby Lake-U) processors.

Hardware details and compatibility status are recorded in the [https://linux-hardware.org/?probe=2f01122616 Linux Hardware Database].

== Webcams and Windows Hello ==

The HP Elite x2 incorporates three cameras connected via MIPI CSI-2 to an Intel IPU3 (CIO2) imaging processor and managed by a Texas Instruments TPS68470 PMIC:
* '''Front RGB Webcam:''' OmniVision OV5670 (5 MP) on CSI-2 Port 1
* '''Rear RGB Camera:''' OmniVision OV8858 (8 MP) on CSI-2 Port 0
* '''Near-Infrared (NIR) Camera:''' OmniVision OV7251 (640x480) on CSI-2 Port 2
* '''IR Illuminator:''' TPS68470 WLED2 driven at 97.5 mA

Mainline kernels do not initialize all three sensors simultaneously due to Intel IPU3 single-DMA receiver limits and PMIC sequencing. A DKMS package and on-demand V4L2 bridge are provided in [https://github.com/ckomma/hp-elite-x2-1012-g2-cameras hp-elite-x2-1012-g2-cameras].

=== Driver Installation ===

Install dependencies:
# pacman -S base-devel dkms v4l2loopback-dkms v4l-utils git

Clone the repository and run the automated installer:
$ git clone https://github.com/ckomma/hp-elite-x2-1012-g2-cameras.git
$ cd hp-elite-x2-1012-g2-cameras
# ./install.sh

The installer performs the following:
# Installs {{ic|hp-camera-unified}} to DKMS, ensuring automated module compilation on future kernel upgrades.
# Configures WirePlumber rules to isolate the loopback device, guaranteeing the front RGB camera defaults in desktop apps (Snapshot, Cheese, Zoom) while preserving rear camera toggling.
# Starts {{ic|hp-ir-feeder.service}}, which listens via inotify to only power up the IR camera and WLED2 illuminator when an authentication request occurs.

=== Howdy (Windows Hello Facial Authentication) ===

Install [[Howdy]] (available in the AUR as {{AUR|howdy}} or {{AUR|howdy-git}}).

Edit {{ic|/etc/howdy/config.ini}}:
<pre>
[video]
device_path = /dev/video20
dark_threshold = 95
use_cnn = true

[debug]
end_report = false
</pre>

{{Note|1=Setting {{ic|dark_threshold = 95}} is essential. In dark rooms, background darkness causes frames to exceed Howdy's default 60% threshold, leading to false "Face detection image too dark" rejections.}}

Add face models:
# howdy -U <username> add

Configure PAM for [[sudo]] in {{ic|/etc/pam.d/sudo}}:
<pre>
auth sufficient pam_python.so /lib/security/howdy/pam.py
</pre>

Configure PAM for GDM screen unlocking in {{ic|/etc/pam.d/gdm-password}}:
<pre>
auth sufficient pam_python.so /lib/security/howdy/pam.py
</pre>

Authentication operates in total darkness using the active TPS68470 WLED2 infrared emitter.
